messages.subject: display(ae)
parts:
Hello.
I get the following when I try to display an ae object:
 
> ae <- ArrayExplorer(cs)
> addColorMap(ae, "sqrt,yellow")    # Immitates dChip's spatial images
> addColorMap(ae, "sqrt,rainbow")  # Very useful to find spatial pattern
> print(ae)
ArrayExplorer:
Name: AnneHelene.xenopus
Tags:
Number of arrays: 25
Color maps: sqrt,yellow; sqrt,rainbow
Path: reports/AnneHelene.xenopus/raw/Xenopus_laevis/spatial
RAM: 0.02MB
> 
> process(ae)
Array #1 ('AH-02202007-1')...
 Color map #1 ('sqrt,yellow')...
 Color map #1 ('sqrt,yellow')...done
...
 
Array #25 ('Lisa_7_Xenopus_laevis')...
 Color map #1 ('sqrt,yellow')...
 Color map #1 ('sqrt,yellow')...done
 Color map #2 ('sqrt,rainbow')...
 Color map #2 ('sqrt,rainbow')...done
Array #25 ('Lisa_7_Xenopus_laevis')...done
[1] FALSE
> display(ae)
Error in function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :
        unable to find an inherited method for function "display", for signature "ArrayExplorer"

 
Also, IE goes bonkers when I try to open ArrayExplorer.html in it. 
 
Thank you.  kv

messages.subject: Re: display(ae)
parts:
Aha, it seems like it is EBImage that causes this (by defining an
already generic function for display()). One possible solution is to
load EBImage *before* aroma.affymetrix, i.e.

library(EBImage)
library(aroma.affymetrix)

Please let use know if this works.

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: display(ae)
parts:
On Mar 6, 3:10 pm, "Karen Vranizan" <vrani...@berkeley.edu> wrote:
> Hello. Yes, loading EBImage first works.

Great. FYI, I am working on an automatic or semi-automatic way to
correct for these types of conflicts (which are beyond
aroma.affymetrix). Keep an eye out for this in the next release.

>
> And Firefox works well, while IE doesn't. Since IE is my default, I would
> need a way to get display to use Firefox, I suppose, or else I would just
> load the html outside of R.

display(ae, ...) of ArrayExplorer uses browseURL() defined in the
'utils' package and passes down any arguments in '...'. See ?
browseURL for details on how to specify what browser you want to use.
There is way for aroma.affymetrix to do this in a generic way that
works on all platforms.

/Henrik

> Thanks!
>
> kv
